cells.tense: You are here with your hands in it, and you know when it is done.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been carrying well past finished. Say out loud that it is done and put it down for the night.
cells.core: You know how to stay with a thing until it stands on its own. You feed it, watch it, adjust what needs adjusting, and you are not guessing while you do it. Care shows up as patience and as work — checking the soil, checking the numbers, checking in. There is a version of this where the step back is as natural as the tending, and that version is probably most of your week.\n\nThe other half is running too. You can tell when something is finished and move your hands off it, which is rarer than knowing how to start. What is behind you no longer asks for anything. Watch yourself do this in the next few hours, because you already are. One step back, then the next thing.
cells.sheetLine: You know when a thing is finished, and you can let it go.
cells.verb: tending what is not finished and letting it be finished
cells.place: the point where work is complete enough to leave your hands

cells.tense: You are already living past the point where this would be finished.
cells.ask: Name one thing that is already done. Do nothing about the next thing for a full day after that.
cells.core: The working version has an end you can feel. You keep something alive, you watch it stand, and then your hands come away — the garden holds without you standing in it. That covers most of what you handle, and you would not call it anything special.\n\nHere it has run past its finish. The work is done and you are still on it, planning how it will hold up, seeing what could still go wrong. Care has turned into holding, and holding has turned into bracing. What you are working out is a future you cannot write in. The thing in front of you is finished. Let that land before you pick up the next one.
cells.sheetLine: You are still holding work that finished without you.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that is already behind you, and it is closed.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you finished and how it went. Let them hear it once, and let that be the ending.
cells.core: When this runs clean it is plain: something gets made, you see that it is made, and you feel the end of it before you start the next. Hands, check, step back — the motion most of your work runs on.\n\nThat motion has stopped. Somewhere the work got set down and not picked back up, and the part of you that would say whether it grew or failed went quiet with it. From the outside it looks like restraint. From in here it is a room you are not standing in, and the finish in front of you stays unfelt, so it does not register as done. Start with one person who will hear it plainly. Say what you made and what happened to it. The point is feeling that the thing has an end you took part in.
cells.sheetLine: You are not in the room where your work finishes.
cells.verb: tending what is not finished and letting it be finished
cells.place: the point where work is complete enough to leave your hands

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in.
cells.ask: Find one thing around you that works because you built it. Say, to yourself, that you made it that way.
cells.core: You keep things going. Plants, schedules, projects, people — they hold because something in you tends them, and you are already calling it maintenance, or the job, or just what has to happen. Said out loud and owned, that hand feeds and then lifts away, and you would name it as yours.\n\nThe author has stepped out of the room. Somewhere along the line, finishing things stopped feeling like yours and started feeling like the work. But the way a thing is raised, the point where you decide it is done or needs more, that is you. Nobody else is holding that pen. Notice when you use it today, and say it, even alone.
cells.sheetLine: The care that holds things up is yours, and you call it maintenance.
